model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата представя групирана стълбовидна диаграма, която илюстрира стойностите на перплексията (Perplexity) при различни нива на разреденост (Sparsity Rate) за два подхода — „Per-Output" и „Per-Layer". Хоризонталната ос е етикетирана като „Sparsity Rate" и съдържа осем категории, подредени в нарастващ ред: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% и 80%. Вертикалната ос е етикетирана като „Perplexity" и използва логаритмична скала, обхващаща диапазон приблизително от стойности малко под 10¹ до 10³, с основни деления при 10¹, 10² и 10³ и допълнителни пунктирани хоризонтални линии за ориентация. За всяка категория на разреденост са представени два стълба — син за „Per-Output" и оранжев за „Per-Layer", както е указано в легендата в горния ляв ъгъл на диаграмата. При ниските нива на разреденост (10%, 20%, 30%) стълбовете и за двата подхода са с много близки и ниски стойности, разположени малко под нивото на 10¹. При 40% и 50% височината на стълбовете леко нараства, но остава в близост до 10¹. При 60% стълбовете достигат стойности около и малко над 10¹, като оранжевият стълб е малко по-висок от синия. При 70% стойностите нарастват значително — синият стълб достига приблизително 20, а оранжевият — около 35–40. При 80% и двата стълба достигат най-високите си стойности — синият е приблизително в диапазона на няколкостотин, а оранжевият се доближава до 10³. Стълбовете не са допълнително визуално подчертани чрез засенчване, удебеляване или анотации извън цветовото кодиране.
model_annotations.Chinese: This chart displays the perplexity values associated with two different methods—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across varying sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the category axis labeled "Sparsity Rate," with categories arranged in ascending order from 10% to 80% at uniform 10% intervals. The vertical axis is labeled "Perplexity" and uses a logarithmic scale, with gridlines visible at powers of ten including 10¹, 10², and 10³, spanning a range from approximately 5 to just under 10³. At each sparsity rate, two bars are grouped side by side: a blue bar on the left representing "Per-Output" and an orange bar on the right representing "Per-Layer," as indicated by the legend in the upper left corner. At 10% sparsity, both bars are very short and nearly equal, each reaching approximately 5 on the perplexity scale. At 20% and 30%, the bars remain similarly low, still close to 5. At 40%, both bars show a slight increase, reaching roughly 6. At 50%, the values rise modestly to around 7–8. At 60%, a more noticeable increase occurs, with the blue bar reaching approximately 10 and the orange bar slightly higher near 12. At 70%, the blue bar reaches roughly 20 and the orange bar approximately 35–40. At 80%, the bars grow dramatically, with the blue Per-Output bar reaching approximately 500–600 and the orange Per-Layer bar approaching nearly 10³ (around 900). The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate from left to right, and the rapid growth at higher sparsity rates is visually prominent due to the logarithmic scale. No bars appear to be specially emphasized through shading, bolding, or annotations beyond the standard color coding.
model_annotations.English: This chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different quantization or pruning strategies, labeled "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer." The horizontal axis represents "Sparsity Rate" with categorical labels at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis represents "Perplexity" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 5 to 10³ (1000), with dashed gridlines at 10¹, 10², and 10³. The chart uses grouped bars at each sparsity rate, with blue bars representing "Per-Output" and orange bars representing "Per-Layer," placed side by side at each category. At 10% sparsity, both bars are very short, with values near 5. At 20% and 30%, the bars remain similarly low, still approximately 5 for both categories. At 40%, the values increase slightly, remaining below 10 for both. At 50%, both bars reach roughly 7–8. At 60%, the bars grow noticeably, with Per-Output at approximately 10 and Per-Layer at approximately 12. At 70%, Per-Output reaches approximately 20 and Per-Layer approximately 35–40. At 80%, the bars are tallest, with Per-Output reaching approximately 500–600 and Per-Layer approaching approximately 900–1000. The bars are not sorted independently but follow the natural ascending order of sparsity rates, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized through outlining, bolding, or annotation beyond the standard color coding described in the legend positioned in the upper left corner of the chart.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm stellt die Perplexität in Abhängigkeit von der Sparsity Rate dar und vergleicht dabei zwei Methoden: „Per-Output" und „Per-Layer". Die horizontale Achse zeigt die Kategorien der Sparsity Rate mit den Beschriftungen 10 %, 20 %, 30 %, 40 %, 50 %, 60 %, 70 % und 80 %, angeordnet in aufsteigender Reihenfolge von links nach rechts. Die vertikale Achse ist mit „Perplexity" beschriftet und verwendet eine logarithmische Skala, die von etwa 1 bis 10³ reicht, mit gestrichelten Hilfslinien bei den Werten 10¹, 10² und 10³. Für jede Sparsity-Rate-Kategorie sind zwei Balken gruppiert nebeneinander dargestellt, wobei der linke blaue Balken die Methode „Per-Output" und der rechte orangefarbene Balken die Methode „Per-Layer" repräsentiert, wie in der Legende oben links angegeben. Bei einer Sparsity Rate von 10 % liegen beide Balken bei einem Perplexitätswert von etwa 5, wobei sie nahezu gleich hoch sind. Bei 20 % und 30 % bleiben beide Balken ebenfalls auf einem ähnlich niedrigen Niveau von ungefähr 5. Bei 40 % steigen die Werte leicht an, wobei beide Balken bei etwa 6 liegen. Bei 50 % erreichen die Balken Werte von ungefähr 7 bis 8. Ab 60 % wird ein deutlicherer Anstieg sichtbar, wobei der blaue Balken bei etwa 10 und der orangefarbene Balken bei etwa 12 liegt. Bei 70 % steigt der blaue Balken auf ungefähr 20 und der orangefarbene auf etwa 35 bis 40. Bei 80 % erreichen die Balken ihre höchsten Werte, wobei der blaue Balken bei ungefähr 500 bis 600 und der orangefarbene Balken bei annähernd 900 bis 1000 liegt. Die Balken sind nicht in absteigender oder anderweitig umsortierter Reihenfolge angeordnet, sondern folgen der natürlichen aufsteigenden Reihenfolge der Sparsity Rate, und es sind keine besonderen visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Umrandungen oder Anmerkungen an einzelnen Balken erkennbar.
